newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-WAUGH AND BLEWETT SHARE CENTURY STAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH AND BLEWETT SHARE CENTURY STAND.

text.p: Steve Waugh and Greg Blewett put Australia in charge of the first test against South Africa on Sunday with an unbroken fifth wicket stand of 110.
The touring team were 284 for four in reply to South Africa's first innings 302 at lunch on the third day.
A cautious start which saw just four runs in the first half hour paid rich dividends for Australia as both batsmen played themselves into a rich vein of form.
South Africa opened their attack with paceman Lance Klusener and wrist spinner Paul Adams before captain Hansie Cronje opted for himself and fellow medium pacer Jacques Kallis.
But Waugh and Blewett gained the upperhand with unerring defence and textook attacking shots.

Waugh survived a bizarre half-chance on 44 when he ducked under a Klusener bouncer only to see the ball hit the back of his bat and fly high to wickletkeeper Dave Richardson who could only touch the ball with his right hand.
Waugh reached his 32nd test half century soon afterwards from 113 deliveries with six boundaries. Waugh was 58 and Blewett 46 at lunch.
